question: Can gating only the active soft preference by the actual setup-search criticality prevent stale low-criticality guidance from disturbing routing, while preserving the stored plan and original native congestion?

evidence.scope: Repeated trajectory events on one seen circuit; existing consumer has no equivalent actual-criticality eligibility gate. Outside DP changed plans and removed96guided-cross evaluations but native heap counts/finalroute/CPD remained unchanged.

method: Separate flag, defaultoff. At the actual setup connection search, use local cost-parameter copy and suppress only method preference when actual criticality is strictly below existing configured planning mincriticality. Do not clear stored guide or replan, prune native edges, alter base congestion/Tdel/STA or RCV. If criticality rises later, same stored plan is available. Explicit native-float boundary handling; eligibility gating is not new delay confidence.
controls: New binary defaultoff exact frozen currentC2/Qs; same parameters, no outside eta/scoring, threshold0 compatibility where applicable. Gate-on count2 and count1 same-setting prefix check. Existing DP/query/delay/source-reverse flags unchanged; no increased budgets. Use actual gated-search/edge contribution counts, all statuses/CPD/tails/SB-CB/iters/planning/probe/fullprocess costs.
qualification: Logical guide eligibility consistency is a hypothesis, not an inferred cause of current CPD degradation. Low-criticality miss events are a small part of total guided crossing work, so measure actual effects before expanding or combining. Outside branch not promoted; do not keep increasing its benefit or query budgets without new evidence.
